# MEDICAL_PRIMITIVES.md — v0.4.4 (DRAFT, not frozen)

The constitution for the PAi Health/Medical engine. Every layer built later
(ingestion, retrieval, LLM, wearables, UI) must conform to this document. If
code and this document disagree, the code is wrong or this document must be
amended explicitly — never silently.

**Read with:** PAi Legal `parliament.py`, `transition_map.py`, `brackets.py`;
canonical `spigot/epifloat.py` and `spigot/bracket_vector.py`;
`fixtures/SCENARIO_001.json`.

**Core vs scaffold.** Anything generated by an external assistant is scaffold
until audited against this document. Scaffold is never evidence about the
system. Golden fixtures are written and verified by hand, never generated.

---

## 0. The central property

> **PAi must refuse to know more than the evidence says.**
>
> What the record says is not what PAi concludes. An authentic document can
> contain a false statement. A chronological relationship is not a causal one.
> Something not found is not something absent. Missing metadata stays unknown.

---

## 1. Primitives and the authority chain

| Primitive | Definition | Created by |
|---|---|---|
| **Float** | One atomic statement or value documented in a source, with exact provenance | Ingestion (deterministic parser, or human-confirmed extraction) |
| **Mix** | A deterministic fact-to-fact relationship between ≥2 Floats | Rule engine only |
| **Gap** | Something sought but not found within an explicitly defined search universe | Rule engine only, against a declared search |
| **Pattern Flag** | A structural observation that Floats/Mixes/Gaps may merit a question | Rule engine only |
| **Stir** | A human-authorized question, evaluated against Float/Mix/Gap and Authority | Opened only per §9 |
| **Authority** | External population-level source (FDA label, guideline, literature) | Retrieval, attached with provenance |

```
Source ─────────→ Float → Mix ─┐
Record search ──────────→ Gap ─┼→ Pattern Flag → [HUMAN GATE] → Stir
External authority ────────────┘                                  │
                                                       SUPPORT / CHALLENGE
```

- Mix consumes Floats only. Gap consumes a declared search over the record set
  only. Pattern Flags consume Floats, Mixes and Gaps.
- Authority enters only at Stir evaluation. It never becomes a Float, Mix, or
  Gap about the patient.
- The HUMAN GATE is hard. Nothing crosses it automatically.

---

## 2. Float

### 2.1 Definition

A Float is exactly one atomic statement or value, as documented, at one
location in one source. A Float records **that the source said it**. It
asserts nothing about whether it is true.

### 2.2 Schema

| Field | Values / rule |
|---|---|
| `float_id` | `FLT-` + hash of canonical content (no timestamps) |
| `patient_id` | Workspace patient |
| `concept` | Normalized concept (vocabulary + code when available, else normalized text) |
| `original_text` | Verbatim span, never rewritten |
| `speaker` | `PATIENT`, `CLINICIAN`, `INTERPRETING_SPECIALIST`, `LAB_INSTRUMENT`, `DEVICE`, `ADMINISTRATIVE`, `FAMILY_OR_OTHER`, `UNKNOWN` |
| `kind` | `REPORT`, `OBSERVATION`, `MEASUREMENT`, `INTERPRETATION`, `ASSESSMENT`, `CODE`, `ACTION`, `MEDICATION_STATUS` |
| `polarity` | `AFFIRMED`, `NEGATED` |
| `certainty` | `DEFINITE`, `HEDGED`, `HYPOTHETICAL` |
| `temporality` | `CURRENT`, `HISTORICAL`, `PLANNED`, `UNSPECIFIED` |
| `experiencer` | `PATIENT`, `FAMILY`, `OTHER` |
| `event_date` | `{value, precision: DAY\|MONTH\|YEAR\|APPROXIMATE\|UNKNOWN, source: DOCUMENTED\|ENCOUNTER_DATE\|DOCUMENT_DATE_FALLBACK\|NONE}` (§2.6) |
| `action_state` | Required for `ACTION`: `PLANNED`, `ORDERED`, `PERFORMED`, `RESULTED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNKNOWN` |
| `medication` | Required for `MEDICATION_STATUS`: see §2.4 |
| `value` | Measurements only (§5) |
| `section` | Note section of the span (HPI, ROS, PMH, Meds, Labs, Exam, Assessment, Plan, Results, Impression, …) |
| `provenance` | `{document_id, document_hash, page, char_start, char_end, author, author_role, signed_date, relay: DIRECT\|TRANSCRIBED}` |
| `root_id` | Provenance root (§4) |
| `provenance_lock` | §3.1 |
| `content_status` | §3.2 |
| `extraction_method` | `PARSER_RULE`, `STRUCTURED_IMPORT`, `HUMAN_ENTRY`, `MODEL_PROPOSAL_CONFIRMED` |
| `standing` | `FIRST_PERSON`, `RELAYED`, `CLINICAL`, `DEVICE` — whose experience it is and how it is used (§18). Independent of both locks |

`relay = TRANSCRIBED` when a value is restated in a document other than its
primary source (a lab value copied into a clinic note). The speaker remains
the original speaker; the primary source is recorded as not provided unless it
is in the record set.

### 2.3 Kind definitions

| Kind | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT` | Someone states their own experience | "numbness began three days after vaccination" |
| `OBSERVATION` | A clinician states what they directly observed | "unsteady gait observed" |
| `MEASUREMENT` | A quantity from an instrument or standardized measure | B12 = 138 pg/mL |
| `INTERPRETATION` | A specialist's reading of a test | "MRI shows no cord lesion" |
| `ASSESSMENT` | A clinician judgment, including history-list entries | "likely pernicious anemia"; "PMH: Type 2 Diabetes" |
| `CODE` | A diagnosis/procedure **code** (ICD, CPT, etc.) | ICD-10 D51.0 on a claim |
| `ACTION` | A non-medication act, with its state | "Plan: check MMA" (`PLANNED`) |
| `MEDICATION_STATUS` | A statement about a medication's status | "Meds: Metformin 1000mg BID" (`LISTED`) |

`CODE` is reserved for actual codes. A diagnosis in text — PMH, problem list,
assessment — is `ASSESSMENT`.

### 2.4 Medication status

Medication presence is not medication action. Every `MEDICATION_STATUS`
Float carries:

| Field | Values / rule |
|---|---|
| `drug` | Normalized name (RxNorm when available) |
| `dose_text`, `route_text`, `frequency_text` | Verbatim from source; null if absent |
| `med_status` | `LISTED`, `REPORTED_TAKING`, `REPORTED_NOT_TAKING`, `PRESCRIBED`, `ADMINISTERED`, `DISPENSED`, `PLAN_START`, `PLAN_CONTINUE`, `PLAN_STOP`, `DISCONTINUED`, `HELD` |
| `start_date` | Only if the source states it; otherwise `UNKNOWN` |

- `LISTED` establishes only that the medication appeared on a list as of the
  document date. It does not establish that it was started, taken, prescribed,
  or administered at that encounter.
- `PLAN_*` values carry `temporality = PLANNED`.
- A medication's start date is never inferred from the date of the document
  that lists it.

### 2.5 Source semantics cannot be strengthened during extraction

A Float's `kind`, `speaker`, `temporality`, `certainty`, `action_state`,
`med_status`, dates and all other semantic fields may not assert more than the
source span establishes. Missing metadata remains unknown.

Examples (all non-exhaustive):

| Source | May not become |
|---|---|
| Medication on a med list | Started, taken, prescribed, or administered |
| Diagnosis in PMH | A `CODE` |
| "PMH" section label | `HISTORICAL` (use the span's own words; otherwise `UNSPECIFIED`) |
| "Plan: check X" | `ORDERED` or `PERFORMED` |
| Performing lab not stated | "Different laboratory" or "same laboratory" |
| Document date | Event, collection, or start date (§2.6) |
| "Around early December" | A `MONTH`-precise or `DAY`-precise date |

### 2.6 Encounter-date rule

| Statement type | `event_date` source |
|---|---|
| About the encounter itself (Exam, ROS, Assessment, Plan, statements made at the visit) | `ENCOUNTER_DATE`, `DAY` precision |
| States its own date ("since 6/18", "around early December 2022") | `DOCUMENTED`, at the precision the text supports |
| Labs, imaging, med lists without a stated collection/start date | `DOCUMENT_DATE_FALLBACK` — an upper bound only ("on or before") |
| No date available | `UNKNOWN` / `NONE` |

### 2.7 Float invariants

1. **One statement, one Float.** "Denies chest pain, SOB, or numbness" yields
   three Floats, each `NEGATED`.
2. **Never inferred.** No exact span → not a Float.
3. **Never rewritten.** Corrections create a new Float linked `SUPERSEDES`.
4. **Classification is by section, not by file.**
5. **Axes are mandatory.** `temporality` may be `UNSPECIFIED` when the span
   does not establish it. `polarity`, `certainty` and `experiencer` must be
   resolved; if they cannot be, the candidate is held in review and is not a
   Float.
6. **Lab flags are interpretations.** An H/L flag printed by the lab is a
   separate `INTERPRETATION` Float. A comparison the engine computes is not a
   Float (§5.3).
7. **Model proposals** enter the ledger only after exact span verification and
   human confirmation.

### 2.8 Negation acceptance cases (must pass before any Mix is built)

| Text | polarity | certainty | temporality | experiencer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ROS: Negative for numbness.` | NEGATED | DEFINITE | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, dizziness, or numbness.` | NEGATED ×5 | DEFINITE | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `Neuro: numbness absent` | NEGATED | DEFINITE | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `Mother had multiple sclerosis.` | AFFIRMED | DEFINITE | HISTORICAL | FAMILY |
| `Rule out B12 deficiency.` | AFFIRMED | HYPOTHETICAL | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `Hx of numbness in 2019, resolved.` | AFFIRMED | DEFINITE | HISTORICAL | PATIENT |
| `Findings not consistent with demyelination.` | NEGATED | DEFINITE | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `No acute distress. Numbness in bilateral feet.` | NEGATED / AFFIRMED (two Floats) | DEFINITE | CURRENT | PATIENT |
| `PMH: Type 2 Diabetes.` | AFFIRMED | DEFINITE | UNSPECIFIED | PATIENT |

PAi Legal's `pattern_is_affirmed` fails rows 1–6 and must not be reused.

---

## 3. The two locks

Every Float, Mix, Gap and Stir evidence item carries two independent fields.
**They are never combined into one score, never averaged, and never displayed
as one indicator.**

### 3.1 Provenance lock — "Did the source actually say this?"

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `VERIFIED_SPAN` | Hash, page and character span re-checked; text matches exactly |
| `UNVERIFIED_EXTRACTION` | Extracted, not yet re-checked |
| `CHECKER_DISCREPANCY` | Page checker or human found disagreement with the page image |
| `FAILED` | Span does not match; Float quarantined |

### 3.2 Content status — "Do we know this statement is true?"

Canonical brackets: `[{UNVERIFIED}]` < `[[SPECULATIVE]]` < `{[EXPLAINED]}` < `[[[VALIDATED]]]`.

1. **Every Float starts `UNVERIFIED`**, regardless of authenticity, speaker,
   or provenance lock.
2. A perfect provenance lock never raises content status.
3. One promotion rule exists: **independent corroboration** (§4.3) → `EXPLAINED`,
   meaning **independently documented**, not biologically established.
4. **`VALIDATED` is unavailable** to the corroboration engine. Any future path
   must be proposition-specific and reviewed before use.
5. **Never promotes:** repetition, pressure, recurrence, model output, document
   count, document rank, user insistence.
6. **Composition floors.** Derived values take the weakest input status
   (canonical `spigot` EpiFloat). Weighted/dominant composition is forbidden.

---

## 4. Provenance roots, copy-forward, independence

### 4.1 Root

`root_id` identifies the **original authoring event of one statement**: the
earliest occurrence of a normalized span, with its author and date. Roots are
assigned **per span, never per document**. Unrelated statements in one note
have different roots.

### 4.2 Copy-forward

A span that reappears later — same normalized text or near-duplicate above a
similarity threshold — shares the root of its first occurrence, **only if**:

1. the normalized span meets a **minimum length** (default 8 tokens,
   `[{calibrated}]`), and
2. the similarity threshold (`[{calibrated}]`) is met and recorded.

Short stock phrases ("denies weakness", "no acute distress") below the minimum
length are **new statements** with new roots: a fresh answer at a new visit is
not copied text.

### 4.3 Independence and corroboration

Two Floats corroborate each other only if **all** hold:

1. Different `root_id`.
2. Different authoring event.
3. Neither is a `REPORT` of the other.
4. **Same referent:** they describe the same event or state at overlapping
   times. Two denials of weakness at two visits are two separate facts, not
   corroboration of one. Two B12 draws are two measurements, not corroboration.

---

## 5. Measurements and comparability

### 5.1 Value block

`{numeric, unit, reference_low, reference_high, reference_unit, specimen, method, performing_lab, collected_at, lab_note}`

- Reference ranges are stored per result, never assumed globally.
- Unknown fields stay null. `performing_lab = null` means **not stated**.
- Values are EpiFloat. Unit conversion factors enter as
  `EpiFloat.structural(...)`, never raw literals.

### 5.2 Comparability classes

| Class | Condition | Allowed |
|---|---|---|
| `COMPARABLE` | Same analyte, unit, and stated lab/method | Delta, trend |
| `CONVERTIBLE` | Same analyte; different unit with a declared structural conversion; same stated lab/method | Delta after logged conversion |
| `CAUTION` | Same analyte, but lab/method differ **or are not stated**, or reference ranges differ | Delta with explicit comparability warning |
| `NOT_COMPARABLE` | Different analyte or specimen, or no declared conversion | No delta. Refuse. |

### 5.3 Engine-computed comparisons

Comparing a value to its own reference range is a deterministic derivation,
not a Float. It is stored on the measurement as
`range_comparison: {result: BELOW|WITHIN|ABOVE, basis: ENGINE_COMPUTED}` and
rendered as "below the reference range reported with the result," never as a
lab flag or a clinical judgment.

---

## 6. Gap

### 6.1 Three different objects

| Object | Example | Primitive |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence of absence | "MRI: no cord lesion" | Float (`INTERPRETATION`, `NEGATED`) |
| Documented non-performance | "B12 not drawn" | Float (`ACTION`, `action_state` per source, `NEGATED`) |
| Not found | No B12 result in the ingested records | **Gap** |

### 6.2 Schema

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `gap_id` | `GAP-` + hash of the search definition and input signature |
| `sought` | Concepts with all aliases and codes used |
| `search_scope` | Exact document IDs searched |
| `date_window` | Explicit start and end dates (open ends stated as such) |
| `coverage` | `{documents_searched, documents_in_window}` |
| `method` | Search method and version |
| `input_signature` | Hash of the record set at search time |
| `result` | `NOT_FOUND` or `NO_RECORDS_IN_WINDOW` |

### 6.3 Rules

1. **Rendering, documents in window ≥ 1:** "Not found in the provided records
   searched ({n} documents searched, {k} dated within {window})."
2. **Rendering, documents in window = 0:** "No records from that period were
   provided ({n} documents searched, 0 in window)." Result
   `NO_RECORDS_IN_WINDOW`. Never "not found."
3. **Forbidden renderings:** "patient did not have X", "X was never done",
   "no history of X", "X was ruled out".
4. A Gap expires when the record set changes and is recomputed.
5. A Gap never changes any content status.

---

## 7. Mix

### 7.1 Definition

A deterministic relationship between ≥2 existing Floats. It creates no Float,
asserts no cause, and needs no hypothesis.

### 7.2 Temporal resolution (every temporal Mix)

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `temporal_resolution` | `EXACT` \| `RANGE` \| `ORDER_ONLY` \| `INDETERMINATE` |
| `delta_days` | Only when `EXACT` |
| `delta_days_min`, `delta_days_max` | Only when `RANGE` |
| `order_basis` | `EVENT_DATES` or `REPORT_SEQUENCE` |
| `date_basis` | Precision and source of each endpoint |

| Endpoints | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Both `DAY`, source `DOCUMENTED` or `ENCOUNTER_DATE` | `EXACT` |
| Bounded intervals (`MONTH`, `YEAR`) that do not overlap | `RANGE` |
| `APPROXIMATE`, or one-sided bound, with order still certain | `ORDER_ONLY` |
| Overlapping intervals, or either end `UNKNOWN` | `INDETERMINATE` |

Rules:

1. `DOCUMENT_DATE_FALLBACK` is an upper bound only and never yields `EXACT`
   or `RANGE`.
2. **Report-sequence ordering.** Two results whose only dates are fallback
   dates from different reports may be ordered by report date:
   `ORDER_ONLY`, `order_basis = REPORT_SEQUENCE`. The basis is rendered
   ("based on the order of the reports").
3. `INDETERMINATE` creates **no** ordering Mix. Conflicting documented dates
   for one event create `DATE_CONFLICT`.
4. Patient-reported approximate onset ("around", "about") is `APPROXIMATE`.
5. Templates per resolution:
   - `EXACT`: "{B} was first documented {n} days after {A}."
   - `RANGE`: "{B} was documented between {min} and {max} days after {A}."
   - `ORDER_ONLY`: "{B} was documented after {A}; the interval cannot be determined from the records."
   - `ORDER_ONLY` + `REPORT_SEQUENCE`: append "(based on the order of the reports)."

### 7.3 Allowed relation enum

| Relation | Endpoints | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `TEMPORAL_PRECEDES` | any → any | §7.2 block |
| `TEMPORAL_COINCIDENT` | any ↔ any | window; `EXACT` or `RANGE` inside window |
| `SYMPTOM_REPORTED_AFTER_EXPOSURE` | `ACTION`/`MEDICATION_STATUS` → `REPORT`/`OBSERVATION` | §7.2 block; exposure date must not be a fallback-only list date |
| `LAB_CHANGED_FROM_PRIOR` | `MEASUREMENT` → `MEASUREMENT` | §7.2 block; comparability class; direction; delta (converted, logged); refuses if `NOT_COMPARABLE` |
| `DIAGNOSIS_RECORDED_AFTER_SYMPTOM` | `REPORT`/`OBSERVATION` → `ASSESSMENT`/`CODE` | §7.2 block |
| `TREATMENT_FOLLOWED_DIAGNOSIS` | `ASSESSMENT`/`CODE` → `ACTION`/`MEDICATION_STATUS` | §7.2 block |
| `SAME_ROOT` | Float ↔ Float | §4.2 evidence (span length, similarity) |
| `INDEPENDENT_AGREEMENT` | Float ↔ Float | passed §4.3 |
| `INDEPENDENT_CONFLICT` | Float ↔ Float | passed §4.3; opposite polarity or incompatible values |
| `DATE_CONFLICT` | Float ↔ Float | same event, different documented dates |
| `SUPERSEDES` | Float → Float | correction |

### 7.4 Mix rules

1. Descriptions from fixed templates only.
2. Forbidden in any Mix name or description: caused, triggered, induced, led
   to, resulted in, due to, because of, secondary to, responsible for,
   attributable to. Verbatim quotes inside a Float's `original_text` are exempt.
3. Mix content status = floor of its endpoints.
4. Treatment response stays sequence; mechanism belongs to Stir.

---

## 8. Pattern Flags

| Flag | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `UNEXPLORED_SEQUENCE` | A temporal chain exists with no `ASSESSMENT` addressing it |
| `UNEXPLAINED_MEASUREMENT_CHANGE` | `LAB_CHANGED_FROM_PRIOR` crossing a reference range with no `ASSESSMENT` referencing it |
| `UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT` | `INDEPENDENT_CONFLICT` or `DATE_CONFLICT` |
| `UNREVIEWED_RESULT` | A result with no later Float referencing it |
| `EXPECTED_ITEM_NOT_FOUND` | A `PLANNED`/`ORDERED` `ACTION` Float plus a Gap for its result |

Rules: fixed templates naming only the cited objects; no diagnosis, mechanism
or disease name unless it is the literal `concept` of a cited Float; a flag
never changes any status.

---

## 9. Hypothesis-opening authority

A Stir may be opened **only** by:

1. **A clinician statement:** an `ASSESSMENT` Float (any certainty) or a
   referral question, stored **verbatim**.
2. **An explicit user question,** stored **verbatim**, including its form as a
   question. "Could X be causing Y?" is never stored as "X is causing Y."

The engine may not rename, sharpen, generalize, or convert a question into an
assertion. A Pattern Flag may be offered to the user ("Ask about this?"); the
user's acceptance and own wording are the opening act. A model may never open
a hypothesis.

---

## 10. Stir evaluation

### 10.1 Structure

- **Subject.** The exposure and the finding named in the proposition are its
  **subject**. Subject Floats are listed separately and **cannot appear in
  SUPPORT**: the thing being explained cannot support its own explanation.
  This is about the proposition's subject, not about subjective vs objective
  evidence.
- **SUPPORT:** items that make the proposition more consistent with the record.
- **CHALLENGE:** items that contradict it or fit an alternative.
- **NON_DISCRIMINATING:** items consistent with both the proposition and a
  documented alternative. Listed in neither channel.
- **No uncited knowledge.** Every item cites a Float, Mix, Gap, or Authority
  ID. An item without an ID is model knowledge and is dropped.

### 10.2 Mandatory CHALLENGE checklist

Each item is answered with cited IDs, or recorded as `NOT_ADDRESSED_NO_SOURCE`:

1. Alternative explanations
2. Pre-existing state
3. Measurement variability
4. Natural history / regression to the mean
5. Concurrent conditions, interventions or exposures (the proposition's own
   exposure is not "concurrent")
6. Timing — including whether the exposure is documented as preceding the
   finding at all
7. Negative findings (weighted equally with abnormal findings)

`NOT_ADDRESSED_NO_SOURCE` renders as "This could not be assessed from the
records and sources provided." An empty CHALLENGE channel never renders as
"no evidence against."

### 10.3 Mechanism chains

When a proposition implies intermediate links (A → B → C):

1. The chain is decomposed into links, each evaluated independently.
2. **Link-source authority.** A link may enter the chain only if it comes
   from (a) an attached Authority, (b) a clinician statement in the record, or
   (c) the user. Each link records its source. A link with no source is not
   added. The engine may not introduce a mechanism on its own.
3. Evidence for one link is never evidence for another. A → B plus B → C
   never silently becomes patient-specific A → C.
4. The output states which links have evidence and which do not.

### 10.4 Klein channel use — EXPERIMENTAL / NOT FROZEN

Off by default. Channel assignment is an unresolved external input
(Engineering OPEN_QUESTIONS, item A). Candidate: A = measured finding,
B = exposure/agent/treatment/authority, C = chronology. If enabled, the fold
only names what is missing. All-channel coverage renders only as: "The record
contains documentation on all three channels. This does not establish a
causal relationship."

### 10.5 Output limits

- Stir reports an evidence map (subject, support, challenge,
  non-discriminating, gaps, chain links), never a verdict.
- Forbidden: confirmed, diagnosed, ruled out, proven, caused, "the patient
  has X".
- Stir content status cannot exceed the floor of the evidence it cites.

---

## 11. Forbidden promotions

| From | To | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Document authenticity | Content status | Authentic documents contain false statements |
| Repetition / copy-forward | Corroboration | Same root is one source |
| Separate events | Corroboration | Different referents (§4.3.4) |
| Pressure / recurrence | Any status | Attention is not truth |
| Gap / empty window | "Absent" / "did not have" | Not found ≠ not present |
| Diagnosis text | `CODE` | Codes are codes |
| Med on a list | Taken / started / prescribed | §2.4 |
| Plan | Ordered / performed | §2.5 |
| Unstated metadata | A stated value | §2.5 |
| Document date | Event / collection / start date | §2.6 |
| `REPORT` | `OBSERVATION` | Patient experience is not clinician observation |
| `HYPOTHETICAL` / `HEDGED` | `DEFINITE` | "r/o X" is not X |
| `FAMILY` | `PATIENT` | Family history is not patient history |
| Temporal Mix | Causal claim | Sequence is not cause |
| Approximate / fallback date | Exact delta | False precision |
| Pattern Flag | Hypothesis | Requires a human opening act |
| User question | Assertion | Verbatim rule (§9) |
| Model output | Float / lock / status / hypothesis / chain link | Model proposes only |
| Authority | Patient Float or patient-specific conclusion | Population-level only |
| Link A→B + link B→C | Patient-specific A→C | §10.3 |
| Independent corroboration | `VALIDATED` | Documentation is not biological truth |
| All Klein channels covered | "Established" | Coverage is not proof |

---

## 12. Rendering rules

1. Findings from record evidence (Part I) are phrased as questions to bring
   to a clinician.
2. Direct suggestions may come **only** from the recommendation library
   (§23) and only after its safety gate passes. Care recommendations come
   only from the lanes (§24). No output ever recommends starting, stopping,
   or changing a **prescribed** treatment or dose, and none ever says a value
   is safe or that care can be skipped.
3. Both locks are shown wherever a status is shown.
4. **Record and Authority are rendered separately.** "Your records document…"
   introduces only Floats/Mixes/Gaps. Authority is introduced separately
   ("Attached medical sources address…") and is always followed by: "These
   sources describe groups of people and do not by themselves establish what
   caused your symptoms."
5. Rendered prose may not contain any fact absent from the computed
   structures (no embellishment: "different labs" when the lab is unknown).
6. Every brief carries: "PAi Health organizes your records, tracks your
   data, and offers general wellness suggestions. It does not diagnose,
   prescribe, or replace your clinician. Decisions belong to you and your
   licensed clinicians."

---

## 13. Determinism and audit

- IDs are hashes of canonical content; no timestamps in identity.
- Every Mix, Gap, Flag and Stir records its rule name and version.
- All derived objects carry the record-set input signature.
- Status changes, opening acts and human confirmations go to the keyed audit
  chain (PAi Legal `audit.py`).
- Same inputs + same rule versions → identical IDs and replay signature.

---

## 14. The model's role

| May | May not |
|---|---|
| Propose Float candidates (§2.7.7) | Create a Float, Mix, Gap or Flag |
| Phrase rendered output from computed structures, within §12 | Add any fact not in the computed structures |
| Suggest search aliases for a Gap (logged) | Set or change either lock |
| Summarize attached Authority with citations | Open a hypothesis or add a chain link (it may *propose* one — see Investigation) |
| Phrase a library suggestion (§23) | Originate a suggestion, threshold, lane, or alert |

Model prose passes through bracket enforcement (PAi Legal `enforce_brackets`)
and the §12 checks before display.

**Investigation (v0.4.3).** Principle: maximum creative freedom, zero authority to
fabricate evidence. The model may explore the computed structures through read-only
tools (search records, read a record and its source text, follow Mixes / roots / Gaps,
query the knowledge base) and may propose anything — hypotheses, questions, tests,
connections — including ideas with no evidence yet. Enforced in code, not by prompt:
- a proposal is a `MODEL_PROPOSAL`, content status `[[SPECULATIVE]]`, and never becomes
  a Float, Mix, Gap, chain link, lock or status;
- cited ids must exist; quotes must match the cited source span word for word;
- §12 wording is enforced; a violation is returned to the model to rephrase, never fixed silently;
- every sentence of its answer cites an id or is a question;
- a proposal reaches the Parliament only when the user asks it as their own question (§9);
- every step (action and result) is stored with the investigation for audit.
In PSi mode investigation needs its own consent scope (§17).

---

## 15. Golden fixtures

1. A golden fixture is a known record set plus its hand-verified expected
   epistemic graph: Floats with all axes, roots, Mixes with resolution, Gaps
   with coverage, Flags, and the Stir map.
2. Fixtures are written and verified by a person. A model may not author the
   expected values.
3. Tests assert **structure exactly** (IDs aside) and **rendering by
   constraint**: required facts present, forbidden phrases absent, no fact
   outside the computed structures.
4. **The build fails** if any parser, rule or model produces a stronger claim
   than the fixture from the same inputs: a promoted status, a sharper date, a
   stronger kind or `med_status`, a merged root, an added chain link, or an
   assertion where the fixture has a question.
5. `fixtures/SCENARIO_001.json` is the first fixture.

---

## 16. Open questions (v0.4)

1. **Copy-forward parameters.** Minimum span length (default 8 tokens) and
   similarity threshold. `[{calibrated}]` until tested on real charts.
2. **Clinician verification as promotion.** Whether, and to what level.
3. **Date-conflict rendering.** Interval vs separate timelines.
4. **Device data.** Aggregation, sampling and authority level for `DEVICE`.
5. **Ontology footprint.** LOINC, RxNorm subset; SNOMED requires UMLS license.
6. **Patient-report challenge.** A `REPORT` with an earlier onset date enters
   CHALLENGE as a `DATE_CONFLICT`; it never edits the clinician Float.
7. **Path to `VALIDATED`.** None exists. Open whether proposition-specific
   criteria could ever justify one.
8. **Klein channel assignment** (§10.4). Test before enabling.
9. **Approximate-date tolerance.** Whether `APPROXIMATE` may carry a declared
   ±n days tolerance allowing `RANGE`. `[{calibrated}]` if adopted.
10. **Authority applicability.** How a population-level Authority's applicability
    to this patient (age, dose, duration) is recorded without the engine
    reasoning beyond the source.
11. ~~Direct-delivery VALIDATED~~ — resolved v0.4.1: user setting (§21.6, §29).
12. **Learned-response thresholds (§21).** N training days and the separation
    test for qualifying a medication's signature. `[{calibrated}]`.
13. **Change-window defaults (§22).** Window length, onset lag, minimum
    readings. `[{calibrated}]` per measure.
14. **Interaction source (§25.5).** Which licensed drug–supplement/herb
    interaction database ships.
15. ~~Live data path~~ — resolved v0.4.1: user setting (§20.4, §29). The
    phone companion is a later build phase; until it ships, only review mode
    is selectable.
16. **Regulatory review.** Early warning, lab suggestions and notifications
    (§24, §28) are the features closest to medical-device territory. Review
    before release.

---

# PART II — THE HEALTH TRACKER (v0.4)

Part I governs record evidence. Part II governs continuous tracking,
suggestions, and notifications. Every Part I rule still applies to every
object Part II creates.

**Design goal (owner's statement):** make suggestions, track change
continuously, and reduce doctor visits — recommending clinician involvement
when the user has followed suggestions over time without change, when an
unexpected change occurs, or when a lane-2/3 rule (§24) applies. Annual
checkups with labs are the baseline (§27).

---

## 17. AI provider modes

| Mode | Provider | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **PAi** | Local model (PAi Legal loader, `local_ai`, `vision.py` page checker) | Default. Nothing leaves the machine. |
| **PSi** | User-supplied API key (NVIDIA Nemotron, OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude; fixed HTTPS endpoints) | Off by default. For phrasing, sends only the minimum computed structures — never documents. **Ingest double-check (v0.4.2):** may send page images with their extracted text and/or the source line of each extracted value, never whole documents, and only for the parts the user switched on for that provider after accepting the consent text (`PSI-INGEST-CONSENT-v1`); consent, scope and withdrawal are audit events; widening the scope asks again. Every call logged in the audit chain (provider, purpose, bytes, images — no content). UI states "health data leaves this computer" whenever on. If the publisher ever supplies the key, a BAA question applies. |
| **None** | No model | Full engine still runs. |

**Invariant:** the engine is deterministic and identical in all three modes.
Every golden fixture must produce the same graph with AI off, PAi, and PSi.
The model's role is §14, nothing more.

---

## 18. Standing

`standing` says whose experience a statement is and how it is used. It is
separate from both locks; brackets keep meaning "independently corroborated."

| Standing | Applies to | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `FIRST_PERSON` | The user's own actions and experiences: doses taken, symptoms, pain scores, meals, self-measured readings | **Accepted as the record** for tracking: counted in adherence, change windows, timelines. Rendered "Logged by you" — never "unverified." |
| `RELAYED` | The user reporting what someone else said ("my doctor said my A1c was 7") | Passed along faithfully, labeled as relayed |
| `CLINICAL` | Clinician, lab, imaging, pathology statements in records | Part I rules |
| `DEVICE` | Sensor output | §20 |

Rules:

1. **The system does not treat the user as suspect.** A user log is never
   downgraded because a sensor did not confirm it.
2. First-person standing covers the user's own actions and experiences, not
   conclusions about cause or diagnosis ("the metformin made me dizzy": the
   dizziness is first-person; the cause is a question).
3. One speaker's logs do not corroborate each other into stronger claims about
   diagnosis or cause (§4 one-speaker rule).

---

## 19. Self-entered data

| Entry | Primitive |
|---|---|
| Symptom diary | `REPORT`, speaker PATIENT, `FIRST_PERSON` |
| Home vitals (cuff, scale, thermometer, strip) | `MEASUREMENT`, speaker PATIENT, device class recorded |
| Dose taken / skipped | `MEDICATION_STATUS: REPORTED_TAKING / REPORTED_NOT_TAKING` |
| Meals | Nutrition log (§25) |
| Lab values typed from a report | `MEASUREMENT`, speaker LAB_INSTRUMENT, relay `TRANSCRIBED`, report image attached |

The entry itself is the source: hashed, immutable, timestamped as its event
date. Edits create `SUPERSEDES`.

---

## 20. Device streams

1. **Raw export or stream is the source.** Daily or windowed summaries are
   derived, carry floor status, and are labeled device-computed.
2. **Device class is recorded on every value** (`WATCH_PPG`, `WATCH_IMU`,
   `HOME_CUFF`, `CGM`, `SMART_SCALE`, `TEST_STRIP`, `SMART_PEN`, `SMART_CAP`,
   …) with a declared authority level per class and measure.
3. **What sensors cover:** watch — heart rate, HRV, sleep, activity, skin
   temperature, SpO₂ (rough). Blood pressure requires a cuff. Continuous
   glucose requires a CGM. No consumer watch measures pH or blood pressure
   reliably.
4. **Live vs review.** Live notifications need data within hours: a phone
   companion (Health Connect / HealthKit) syncing to the desktop. Without it,
   the same logic runs as after-the-fact review. The user chooses (§29,
   `data_path`).

   **Phone companion (v0.4.4).** Android app reading Health Connect (read only).
   - **Network exception.** The UI server stays loopback-only. A second listener exists only while
     the user turns the companion on; it binds to the computer's private home-network address
     (RFC 1918 only, never 0.0.0.0 or a public address), answers only ping / hello / sync, and only
     accepts bodies sealed with a paired phone's key.
   - **Pairing** is by QR code shown on the computer (single use, 10 minutes). The secret never
     travels over the network. Every body is AES-256-GCM sealed with HKDF-derived per-direction
     keys, bound to its path; a strictly increasing sequence number refuses replays.
   - **The phone runs the same fixed rules** the computer sends it (§21.3 prompts with the §21.4
     line, the severe-reading recheck, the lane-3 text), so prompts arrive on time while the
     computer is off. Phone logs are FIRST_PERSON and queue on the phone until synced; the vault
     is the record. A locked computer accepts nothing.
   - `data_path = LIVE` is available only once a phone is paired.
5. No device output is ever rendered as proof of a diagnosis or cause.
6. **Bluetooth LE (v0.4.2).** Standard Bluetooth SIG health profiles only (heart rate, blood
   pressure, thermometer, weight scale, pulse-oximeter spot check). Every raw packet is kept in
   the encrypted vault beside its decode; device class comes from the profile the device exposes;
   a reading uses the device's own time stamp when the packet carries one, otherwise the receive
   time, and says which. Glucose meters are captured raw only until a meter is validated.

---

## 21. Medication verification by expected response

### 21.1 Learn

For each medication, on days with a logged dose, measure what the user's own
data does in a declared post-dose window ("on dose days resting HR falls about
8 bpm within 2 hours"). The expectation is learned from the user's data and
cites it. No drug knowledge is assumed.

### 21.2 Qualify

After N logged dose days `[{calibrated}]`, test whether dose days separate from
non-dose days. If not: "No reliable pattern found for this medication;
reminders will use your schedule only." Typically detectable: beta-blockers
(HR), insulin (CGM), stimulants (HR), some BP medicines with frequent
readings. Typically not: metformin, statins, levothyroxine, most maintenance
drugs.

### 21.3 Watch and prompt

| At scheduled dose time + window | Action |
|---|---|
| Pattern seen, dose logged | Nothing |
| Pattern seen, no log | "Looks like you may have taken your 8am dose. Log it?" |
| No pattern, no log | "Your usual post-dose pattern hasn't shown up yet. Did you take your 8am dose?" (Yes / No / Not sure) |
| No pattern, dose logged | Nothing. The log stands (§18). |

### 21.4 Double-dose safety (hard-coded)

No message ever tells the user to take a dose. Every dose prompt ends:
"If you're not sure whether you took it, check your medication's instructions
or ask your pharmacist before taking another dose."

### 21.5 Optional sensor confirmation

| Sensor class | Confirms |
|---|---|
| Direct delivery (smart pen, inhaler sensor) | Dose dispensed |
| Container access (smart cap, dispenser) | Container opened — not swallowed |
| Physiological signature | Consistent pattern only, never a specific dose |
| Motion gesture | Hint only |

Sensors only add ("also recorded by your pill cap"). A missing sensor event
never flags or downgrades a log. A sensor event with no log becomes a prompt;
nothing is auto-logged.

### 21.6 Direct-delivery VALIDATED path (user setting)

When the user enables `device_dose_confirmation` (§29): proposition "dose
delivered at time t" + matching direct-delivery sensor event (smart pen,
inhaler sensor) within declared tolerance → `VALIDATED`, scoped to that single
dose event.

1. Applies to direct-delivery sensors only. Container access stays `EXPLAINED`;
   physiological signatures never confirm a dose.
2. Scope never widens: a validated dose event says nothing about adherence on
   other days, absorption, or whether the medication is working.
3. Every object it affects records the setting and rule version; exports and
   briefs label it "confirmed by device (user setting)" so a clinician knows
   how the status arose.
4. Turning the setting off re-evaluates affected events back to `EXPLAINED`
   (or `FIRST_PERSON` accepted); history of the change is kept in the audit
   chain.
5. Golden fixtures involving dose events run with the setting both on and off.

---

## 22. Medication change windows

1. **Anchor:** a medication event with a source-supported date (documented or
   user-logged start, stop, dose change). `LISTED` with a fallback date cannot
   anchor.
2. **Targets:** measures set by the user, the clinician, or an attached
   Authority. The engine never decides on its own what a medication should
   affect.
3. **Computation:** pre-window and post-window of N days `[{calibrated}]`,
   optional onset lag, minimum K readings each (else "too few readings to
   compare"), comparable device class only, change shown against the
   pre-window's own day-to-day spread, adherence from logged doses.
4. **Mandatory challenge items:** other changes in the window; regression to
   the mean (flag when the anchor followed a spike); measurement change
   (device, time of day); adherence unknown.
5. **Side effects** use the same machinery in reverse:
   `SYMPTOM_REPORTED_AFTER_EXPOSURE`, sequence only.
6. **Never rendered:** "the medication works," "the dose is too low," "you can
   stop it," any dosing suggestion.

---

## 23. Recommendation library and workup

### 23.1 Library entries

Modeled on PAi Legal's jurisdiction rule packs: curated, versioned, cited,
applied deterministically.

```
id, version
trigger:            deterministic condition over the user's data
suggestion:         fixed text (model may rephrase only)
source:             guideline/label, URL, verified_as_of
required_inputs:    measures/records needed before showing
warrant:            cited reason each required input matters
contraindications:  record conditions / meds / suspected patterns that suppress it
expected_effect:    as stated by the source, with population caveat
lane:               §24 lane it may appear in
```

### 23.2 Workup flow

1. Trigger fires from the user's data.
2. Required inputs checked; missing ones are Gaps.
3. Missing **home-measurable** inputs become an information-gathering request
   (strip, cuff, scale, thermometer, watch), with technique instructions.
4. Missing **lab** inputs become a lab suggestion (§23.3).
5. Results gate only: show, suppress, or route to clinician. A result never
   produces a diagnostic label.
6. The warrant for every request comes from the entry's cited source, never
   engine intuition.

### 23.3 Lab suggestions

1. Only from a cited library entry (e.g. periodic B12 testing for people on
   long-term metformin, especially with neuropathy).
2. Patterns, not single readings; the entry declares count and period.
3. Worded as a reason to ask: "ask your clinician about a kidney function
   test" — never "you need labs," never naming a disease.
4. Urgency from cited thresholds: routine / soon / urgent (§24).
5. Labs never replace a visit; results never clear someone to skip one.
6. Direct-to-consumer lab results are imported as Floats, shown against
   printed ranges, and out-of-range items become clinician questions.
7. Returning results fill the Gap and re-evaluate the trigger.

### 23.4 Information-gathering devices

Home-safe only. Multi-parameter urine strips (glucose, protein, blood, ketones,
leukocytes, nitrites, pH) are preferred over pH-only strips. Strip readings are
coarse; repeated readings are required and a single reading is never used
alone.

---

## 24. Early warning and the three lanes

### 24.1 Triggers (all cited)

- **Data-pattern triggers:** persistent readings outside cited thresholds.
- **Schedule triggers:** age/sex/risk-based screenings due (USPSTF, ADA).

### 24.2 Lanes

| Lane | Examples | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Lifestyle first** (default) | Stage 1 BP, mildly high home glucose, weight, sleep, activity, stress | Suggestions + tracking only. Clinician prompt only when (a) the user confirms following the plan over the entry's declared window and change-window math shows no change beyond normal variation, or (b) an unexpected change occurs. |
| **2 — Lifestyle + check-in** | Persistent BP ≥140/90; fasting glucose repeatedly ≥126 or glucose on strips; repeat protein/blood on strips; unexplained weight loss; persistent symptoms | Suggestions run immediately **and** one calm clinician prompt shows in parallel. Dismissible; stays visible but quiet; no nagging. Never suppressed while the pattern holds. |
| **3 — Urgent** | BP ≥180/120 with symptoms, chest pain, sudden weakness, breathing trouble | Fixed emergency message only. No suggestions. |

Thresholds above are illustrative; each lives in a cited library entry.

### 24.3 Rules

1. **Unexpected change escalates immediately** regardless of adherence:
   worsening values or new symptoms move to lane 2 or 3.
2. **Persistence before flagging** (declared count/period); urgent symptoms
   skip the wait.
3. **Device quality counts.** Low-authority device data alone (e.g. watch
   SpO₂) never triggers lane 2/3; it prompts a recheck with a better device.
4. **Name the check, not the disease.** "These tests check how well your
   kidneys are working."
5. **Suspected counts as confirmed for safety.** While a kidney, cardiac or
   glucose pattern is unresolved, contraindicated suggestions stay held.
6. **Voluntary.** The system recommends; the user decides.

---

## 25. Nutrition and natural balancing

### 25.1 Logging

Manual search and barcode matched to USDA FoodData Central (public domain,
offline). Photo logging: local vision model proposes foods and portions; the
user confirms. Totals carry a range; no false precision.

### 25.2 Targets

Dietary Reference Intakes and Dietary Guidelines as cited baselines.
**Clinician plans override** for kidney disease, heart failure, diabetes carb
plans and pregnancy; if the record shows one and no plan exists, the system
asks for one rather than improvising.

### 25.3 Scope

| Included (cited, trackable) | Excluded (no evidence base) |
|---|---|
| Sodium/potassium balance; blood-sugar stability (meal composition, timing, CGM); fiber; protein distribution; hydration within clinician limits; meal timing vs sleep; micronutrient gaps vs DRIs, lab-confirmed where possible | Alkaline diet / body pH balancing; detox and cleanses; "adrenal fatigue" protocols |

### 25.4 Personal response loop

Change windows and pattern rules applied to food: glucose response by meal
(CGM), BP vs logged sodium, food–symptom sequences ("bloating logged after 4 of
5 dairy meals") shown as sequence only, never as an intolerance diagnosis.

### 25.5 Food–drug interaction gate

Runs against the medication list before any suggestion: grapefruit with some
statins and calcium-channel blockers; vitamin K consistency on warfarin;
potassium foods and salt substitutes with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone;
calcium/iron timing with levothyroxine and some antibiotics; tyramine with
MAOIs; alcohol with metformin. Each a cited entry, mostly FDA labels.

### 25.6 Supplements — food first

Suggested only when a lab shows deficiency, a clinician directs it, or the
user asks. Every supplement passes the medication-interaction check and the
upper-limit check. Herb–drug interactions require a licensed database (open
question 14).

### 25.7 Disordered-eating safeguards (always on)

No targets below safe floors. Very low intake or rapid weight loss stops any
lower-target suggestion and shifts to neutral support plus a clinician
question. Calorie display can be hidden. Age gate for minors.

---

## 26. Template condition: blood pressure

Every condition follows this shape: pattern → measurement check → cited
natural suggestions behind the gate → feedback loop → lane rules in parallel.

1. **Measurement check first:** seated, back supported, 5 minutes rest, arm at
   heart level, correct cuff size, two readings morning and evening, validated
   cuff (validatebp.org).
2. **Suggestions** (average effects per the ACC/AHA high blood pressure
   guideline; figures verified against the source when entries are written):

| Suggestion | Typical systolic effect | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| DASH-style eating | ~11 mmHg | Kidney concern → clinician first |
| Sodium reduction | ~5–6 | — |
| Potassium from food | ~4–5 | Suppressed with ACE-i/ARB/spironolactone, kidney concern (suspected or confirmed), or no kidney labs (§27); salt substitutes blocked likewise |
| Aerobic activity ~150 min/week | ~5–8 | Chest pain/symptoms → hold; BP ≥160/100 → moderate only until checked |
| Resistance / isometric training | ~4–5 | Same |
| Weight loss if overweight (~1 mmHg per kg) | varies | Off under §25.7 safeguards |
| Limit alcohol | ~4 | — |
| Sleep and stress routines | supportive | — |

3. **Logged items that raise BP** (NSAIDs, decongestants, heavy caffeine):
   "Some of what you've logged can raise blood pressure; ask your pharmacist
   about alternatives." Never "stop taking X."
4. **Feedback:** change window per adopted habit.
5. Already on BP medication: suggestions are additions, never "you may not
   need your medication."
6. Lane rules (§24) run in parallel throughout.

---

## 27. Annual labs

1. **Annual checkup with labs is a required input.** The list is set per user
   from cited cadence rules (USPSTF, ADA) and framed as "ask your clinician to
   include": metabolic panel (kidney, liver, electrolytes) for everyone; A1c or
   fasting glucose, lipids, urine albumin-to-creatinine by age and risk; B12,
   CBC, thyroid, vitamin D when data or medications call for it.
2. **Without this year's labs everything runs**, with one standing notice:
   "This year's labs haven't been entered. Kidney function, cholesterol,
   thyroid and similar can't be monitored, and suggestions are based on your
   device and logged data only."
3. **Fixed hold list** — the only suggestions held without labs:

| Held until | Suggestion |
|---|---|
| Kidney function known | More potassium / potassium supplements |
| Kidney function known | Salt substitutes (potassium chloride) |
| Kidney function known | High-protein plans |
| Relevant level known | Iron supplements |
| Relevant level known | High-dose vitamin D |

   Shown as "available once kidney function (or the relevant level) is known."
   Fasting with insulin or sulfonylureas is blocked by the medication list,
   not labs.
4. **Entry:** PDF/photo through Part I ingestion with page checker; manual
   typing as relay `TRANSCRIBED` with the report image attached; patient-portal
   FHIR import when built.
5. Labs feed baselines, change windows, lane gating, early warnings, nutrition
   gates and workup closure.

---

## 28. Notification boundary

1. All alert and prompt logic is deterministic; a model never decides to
   notify or what threshold applies.
2. Notifications never: say a value is safe or normal-for-you as a reason to
   skip care; tell the user to take, skip, or change a dose; name a disease.
3. Lane-3 messages are fixed text, not rephrased by a model.
4. Every notification records its rule ID and version in the audit chain.

---

## 29. User settings that change engine behavior

Settings that alter statuses, triggers or notifications are few, explicit,
and auditable.

| Setting | Options | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data_path` | `REVIEW` (desktop, after-the-fact) / `LIVE` (phone companion) | `REVIEW` | Live enables §21.3 real-time dose prompts and §24 live alerts; review runs the same rules on imported data with a "found in review" label |
| `device_dose_confirmation` | Off / On | Off | §21.6 |
| `ai_mode` | None / PAi / PSi | PAi if a local model is installed, else None | §17 |

Rules:

1. Every setting change is written to the audit chain with time and old/new
   value.
2. Every derived object records the settings in force when it was computed;
   the input signature includes them.
3. No setting can lower a safety rule: lane 3, the double-dose rule (§21.4),
   the hold list (§27), interaction gates (§25.5) and disordered-eating
   safeguards (§25.7) are not configurable.

---

> **Float records what was said. Mix records how facts relate in time and
> quantity. Gap records what was looked for and not found. Only a person opens
> a question. Stir maps the evidence on both sides — and stops there.**
>
> **The tracker suggests from cited rules, measures what changes, and says
> plainly when it is time to involve a clinician.**
